evidence.note: Create Agent calls save; validation and in-progress state can disable the button.
The editor submits the prepared draft to ScheduleModel.saveSchedule and displays a save failure.
Save validates the draft, optionally includes a workflow, POSTs or PATCHes the schedule, then updates the list and refreshes session metadata.
Draft and existing-task checks require available workspace, model, team and account as applicable; intervals are bounded.
AppModel configures ScheduleModel with the backend, validation, refresh, queued-run admission and workflow capability closures.
Registers create, list, update, dispatch, occurrence and history endpoints.
The domain route registry includes the schedules module and invokes its register_routes function.
Creation checks capability gates, persists a validated schedule, creates its dedicated chat and removes the schedule if chat creation fails.
Disabled API capabilities reject the request; workspace must exist, and worktree schedules require a Git workspace.
Recurrence validation supports once, daily, weekdays, weekly and bounded intervals.
Schedule validation checks fields, runner, provider/account, model, timezone and a future next occurrence.
RunStore validates schedule/workflow data and inserts schedule configuration and next-run time, then returns the saved row.
Schedule creation or dispatch reuses a dedicated session or creates one, persists schedule-linked metadata and returns it.
Runtime tick scans due enabled schedules at a five-second minimum cadence, gated by controller presence or keep-running configuration, dispatches and queues returned runs.
Runtime coordinator invokes automation tick unless paused/in maintenance, respects execution limits and waiting states, and preserves a single writer per workspace.
Dispatch holds a schedule lock, claims an occurrence, prepares the dedicated session and skips when that chat has an active run.
Occurrence claim uses an immediate transaction, deterministic due-occurrence IDs, and advances cadence before outside work.
When workflow capability and stored workflow are present, schedule dispatch calls start_execution, associates occurrence state/run and returns the result.
Creates an execution snapshot, advances to its next action, queues an agent action and synchronizes origin status.
A run_agent action creates a deterministic run ID, queues the run with schedule metadata, binds it to the workflow step and returns it.
Workflow advancement prepares an agent prompt, marks awaiting_run and returns the first agent action.
Non-workflow schedules queue a run, persist occurrence linkage and return; failures record an error and selected workspace errors pause the schedule.
Busy chats record skipped occurrences; a one-time slot is rearmed, and idle-check plus queue reservation is atomic in the store.
Occurrence updates persist state, chat/run links and errors; skipped overlaps do not overwrite the schedule last-run/error summary.
Queued run loads saved route/profile/account configuration, waits for missing prerequisites, applies provisioned permissions, builds a user_message and enqueues it.
Supervisor starts or reuses a worker, resumes the dedicated session and opens its /ws/chat transport.
Supervisor stores queued command intent and private command configuration.
Coordinator applies runtime configuration, marks the queued command sent/running and sends it to the worker.
Supervisor send serializes the command over the worker WebSocket.
User-message handling selects saved-profile, team or normal turn handling, persists pending input and starts the turn with an acknowledgement.
Saved-profile turn enters its profile boundary and calls the ordinary user-turn function.
User-turn execution invokes AgentCore.run_turn with text, permission decision callback and tool eligibility.
Worker events persist approval/native-tool decisions and set waiting_approval or waiting_for_locus; turn completion releases the active command and events are published.
When the controller disconnects, workers lacking keep-running are interrupted and paused.
Schedule editor explains permission policy and that requests requiring approval pause the run.
Legacy desktop scheduling polls every 30 seconds but is bypassed when the independent runtime is enabled.
Inspector selects schedule history endpoint and decodes the returned history page.
Loaded inspector results update the published snapshot/cache; failed refresh retains the last saved information.
History endpoint returns the schedule-scoped history page; occurrence detail returns execution links and delivery/execution state.
History joins schedule occurrences to run and workflow execution state, scopes by agent ID and returns paginated rows/counts.
RunStore opens SQLite with foreign-key enforcement for record operations.
durable_runs and automation_workflows_v1 have named environment gates; actual deployed values were not inspected.
Runtime watches workflow run terminal states, calls complete_step with result/error and queues any following run.
Workflow origin synchronization updates the schedule occurrence; synchronization failure is best effort and does not repeat an action.

changes.goal: Change which recurrence patterns an agent can use
changes.explanation: Keep recurrence validation/calculation and the desktop’s draft checks consistent; callers depend on the saved next-run time.

changes.goal: Change how overlapping scheduled runs are handled
changes.explanation: The dispatcher skips a busy conversation and uses durable occurrence claims. Changing overlap behavior affects cadence, history and the one-time rearm path.

changes.goal: Change when scheduled work can keep running
changes.explanation: Due dispatch and worker admission both check controller presence or keep-running policy; waiting states and workspace concurrency also affect admission.

sections.title: When recurring work can run
sections.text: The independent runtime checks due schedules at a five-second minimum cadence while it is active. Dispatch requires a connected controller or keep-running permission for the automation. The legacy desktop coordinator checks every 30 seconds and is disabled when the independent runtime is enabled. This establishes code paths, not that a particular machine’s runtime is installed, awake or provisioned.

sections.title: What can stop a scheduled run
sections.text: Schedule creation requires a valid future recurrence, an available workspace, and a configured model/account; worktree execution requires a Git workspace. A busy dedicated chat causes a skipped occurrence, with one-time slots rearmed. Missing account/profile prerequisites wait for attention, and runtime approval/native-tool requests enter waiting states. Stored workflows take their workflow path; older definitions use the direct queued-run path.

sections.title: Where recurring work is remembered
sections.text: Each scheduled agent has a persistent dedicated chat. Occurrences are separately linked to runs/workflow executions, and the inspector requests a paginated history scoped to that schedule. Workflow origin synchronization is best effort; the execution record remains authoritative. A saved history row does not establish that every requested external effect succeeded.

coverage.explanation: Read targeted ranges in 15 implementation files covering desktop creation, recurrence validation, durable claims, stored-workflow first-step admission, runtime eligibility, permission waits and history retrieval. No application, scheduler or provider was executed.
uninspected: Live runtime installation and enabled capability/account settings
Complete multi-step workflow branches and team-run execution
Actual provider responses, notifications and external effects
All recurrence edge cases and recovery paths; source was inspected but tests were not run

uncertainties.question: Is the user’s actual runtime installed, running and provisioned to execute this schedule when the desktop is closed?
uncertainties.reason: Source contains controller/keep-running, account/profile and maintenance gates. Private state and live services were deliberately not read or exercised.
uncertainties.next_step: If operational confirmation is needed, inspect the app’s runtime and scheduled-agent status with the user’s intended schedule.

uncertainties.question: How does each configured later step finish, and what exact result appears for the user?
uncertainties.reason: First-agent-step admission and history read paths are traced. Follow-up reconciliation calls were located, but their complete execution-state transitions and notifications were outside the bounded inspection.
uncertainties.next_step: Focus on the chosen agent’s workflow and trace completion events through run state, workflow advancement and inspector presentation.
